item.title: Lake Murray dries up as severe drought hits PNG’s Western Province
item.description: Thousands of residents in Papua New Guinea's Western Province are facing severe water shortages, school closures, and rising disease as the country’s largest lake dries up during a prolonged dry spell. item.content:encoded:
Thousands of residents in Papua New Guinea's Western Province are facing severe water shortages, school closures, and rising disease as the country’s largest lake dries up during a prolonged dry spell.

Island communities in the Lake Murray local level government area of Middle Fly District are being forced to abandon their homes and camp near shrinking creeks as surrounding lagoons dry out completely.

Middle Fly District acting disaster coordinator Jeremiah James said water levels at the Lake Murray outlet into the Herbert River have dropped by two metres, leaving gravel bars exposed and blocking river travel for dinghies and canoes.

The drop in water levels has halted river trade to the nearby hub of Obo, forcing local trade stores to shut down operations.

With water routes blocked, the only remaining access route for essential goods is the Aimbak-Kewe road, where hiring a vehicle now costs K600 one way.

Fuel prices in Lake Murray have also surged to K12 per litre.

Health workers in the region have reported an increase in cases of stomach pain, diarrhoea, malaria, typhoid, and other waterborne diseases.

Local authorities have confirmed that island schools in the Lake Murray area have closed down.

Lake Murray leaders say the situation is worsening rapidly and requires urgent intervention from both provincial and national authorities.

"Super El-Niño is real," a local resident from Boboa station told NBC News . "If the dry spell continues, people at Boboa station will leave for inland areas to find water and food."

James said the provincial disaster office will bypass initial assessments to expedite emergency relief.

"The plan from the Disaster Office is that we will not go and do assessments first," Mr James said. "We are planning immediate relief supply needs."

Community leaders say short-term aid will not solve the recurring crisis, urging the national and provincial governments to invest in long-term water security projects, including rainwater harvesting and permanent catchment systems.

item.title: NCC partners East Sepik to strengthen cultural preservation and boost tourism
item.description: The National Cultural Commission [NCC] has formalised a partnership with the East Sepik Provincial Government through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] aimed at preserving and promoting the province's rich cultural heritage. Under the agreement, the NCC presented K500,000 to support cultural preservation initiatives, traditional practices, and activities that promote East Sepik's
item.content:encoded:
The National Cultural Commission [NCC] has formalised a partnership with the East Sepik Provincial Government through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] aimed at preserving and promoting the province's rich cultural heritage.

Under the agreement, the NCC presented K500,000 to support cultural preservation initiatives, traditional practices, and activities that promote East Sepik's unique identity.

Speaking during the signing ceremony, Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture, Belden Namah said protecting Papua New Guinea's diverse culture is a national priority, with many traditional customs and practices at risk of disappearing.

He said the ministry is supporting provinces with K500,000 and districts with K300,000 to strengthen cultural preservation efforts and ensure future generations continue to value and practice their cultural heritage.

East Sepik Governor Allan Bird, who welcomed the partnership, said it as a significant investment in safeguarding the province's cultural identity. He thanked the minister for the support, stating that it is the largest cultural funding the province has received from a national ministry.

"The province is committed to working closely with the National Cultural Commission to preserve East Sepik's cultural heritage while creating opportunities to promote tourism through culture," Bird said.

He also called for better coordination between the provincial government and the ministry, saying all cultural funding requests should be channelled through the province and that cultural events should align with the national cultural Commission calendar to improve planning and maximize support.

The partnership marks a significant step in strengthening collaboration between the National Cultural Commission and the East Sepik Provincial Government to ensure the province's rich cultural traditions are preserved and celebrated for generations to come.

item.title: Remote Pale village in SHP lights up with PNG power
item.description: The remote Pale village of Kewabi LLG within the Ialibu/Pangia district in Southern highlands province has finally lit up by PNG power supply on Thursday afternoon. item.content:encoded:
The remote Pale village of Kewabi LLG within the Ialibu/Pangia district in Southern highlands province has finally lit up by PNG power supply on Thursday afternoon.

Under the Rural Electrification Program, Southern Highlands Provincial Government (SHPG, PNG Power based in Ialibu, Project manager, Kessy Nape inspected and approved the rural electrification project and switched on the power source for the first time in the small community.

Community leader, Siro Yoko thanked governor William Powi for making funds available.

"Although power already reached the main center of Pale village, a three phase power supply must completely reach out to areas of Kuni, Yokere, Rala and Kambi which makes up the whole Pale community within the two council wards of Pale One and Two.

“This extension work will need extra funding which he appealed for support to Governor Powi, Ialibu/Pangia District Development Authority and others to support.” Yoko said.

Kewabi LLG president, Francis Walipe thanked governor Powi and asked the community to embrace the service delivery and look after the power project.

Ialibu PNG Power office Manager, Mr. Jim Kewa appealed to the community to look after the power, follow safety protocols and started coming to office for power connectivity into their homes.

He further warned the community of illegal power connections as laws are there to prosecute anyone and encouraged them to pay bills faithfully.

Governor William Powi committed a K5 million for this vital power project from Yarena to Pale villages for almost fifteen (15) kilometers of road distance. The actual funding was made in 2024 which a private eletrical contractor, Tagali Construction Company was engaged into Pale community.

item.title: Catholic Jubilee celebrations in Kieta continues at Pokpok Island
item.description: Catholic faithfuls are being ferried across to Pokpok Island in Kieta, to join a foundation service later this morning to mark the arrival of the Catholic Church in Bougainville. Two Marist priests landed in 1901 and said the first mass on Pokpok, later spreading the gospel across the region.
item.content:encoded:
Catholic faithfuls are being ferried across to Pokpok Island in Kieta, to join a foundation service later this morning to mark the arrival of the Catholic Church in Bougainville.

Two Marist priests landed in 1901 and said the first mass on Pokpok, later spreading the gospel across the region.

Visiting bishops, priests and other missionaries have been accorded a 'dutasisi' or a Kieta traditional welcome at Tubuiana Parish yesterday afternoon as the hours count down to the Central Bougainville leg of the 125 Years Jubilee Celebrations of the Catholic faith in Bougaimville.

The visiting religious dignitaries include Archbishop of East New Britain Rochus Tatamai, Archbishop of Mt. Hagen Clement Papa, Fr. Harry Moore, Fr. Phil Gibbs President of Divine Word University, and other missionaries.

Bishop of Bougainville Diocese Darius Kalusza, says the Jubilee is not only for the Central Deanery, but for the entire region, adding that Bougainville must first seek the kingdom of God and all its wish will be added to it, making particularly reference to the region's political push for independence.

Pokpok is 6.6 km² in size and is predominantly Catholic.

The island's permanent church was rebuilt months ago, after the original structure built following the missionaries landing was burnt down at the height of the Bougainville Crisis.

Faithfuls have come from across the Central Bougainville Deanery as well as from the Southwest and North (Buka-Atolls) Deanery to join in the celebrations.

This morning's celebratory service will be held at the exact sight where the first mass was held, on the beachfront.

item.title: Ahi indigenous workers take up job opportunities in Australia
item.description: Five more Ahi indigenous people from Lae, including one woman, are preparing to leave for Australia this weekend under the Lae Labour Mobility Program. The workers are among 21 Papua New Guineans selected for jobs with a casino food company in New South Wales.
item.content:encoded:
Five more Ahi indigenous people from Lae, including one woman, are preparing to leave for Australia this weekend under the Lae Labour Mobility Program.

The workers are among 21 Papua New Guineans selected for jobs with a casino food company in New South Wales.

Before their departure, the workers completed their oath and declaration at the Lae City Authority.

The latest group adds to the growing number of Ahi people accessing overseas employment opportunities. Nine Ahi workers are already working in Australia, while five more, including one female worker, will travel this weekend.

Lae City Authority representative Margaret Gelam said the program is giving Ahi people an opportunity to gain new skills, support their families and return with experience that can benefit their community.

Team leader Kekeng Nicky Kawambara said the program is creating pathways for more Ahi people to enter the workforce and improve their livelihoods.

Ahi representative Elizabeth Sinemau said the workers’ success shows the importance of providing opportunities for Indigenous communities.

She encouraged the workers to remain committed, work hard and proudly represent the Ahi community, Lae and Papua New Guinea while overseas.

The Lae Labour Mobility Program continues to create employment pathways for Ahi families through overseas work, skills development and income opportunities.

item.title: Fly Zibo communities dig channels by hand as drought dries river
item.description: Communities in the newly created Fly Zibo local level government [LLG] area of Middle Fly district, Western, are facing a severe humanitarian crisis, forcing residents to manually dig water channels as a 10-week drought continues to dry up major waterways. All nine wards in Fly Zibo rely entirely on the Fly River and surrounding lagoons for drinking water, food and transport.
item.content:encoded:
Communities in the newly created Fly Zibo local level government [LLG] area of Middle Fly district, Western, are facing a severe humanitarian crisis, forcing residents to manually dig water channels as a 10-week drought continues to dry up major waterways.

All nine wards in Fly Zibo rely entirely on the Fly River and surrounding lagoons for drinking water, food and transport.

However, prolonged dry weather conditions have dropped water levels to critically low levels, closing vital river shortcuts to Obo and Kiunga and turning once-navigable lagoons into mud flats.

Locals say lives are at risk as people are forced to walk long distances to reach the main Fly River channel.

The cost of fuel in the area has surged to K12 per litre, while the movement of essential food and goods has completely stopped.

Island schools across the LLG have been forced to close, although teachers remain in the communities awaiting further direction from provincial education authorities.

“The river that feeds us is dying. We are digging just to find water,” one community member said.

Fly Zibo LLG is currently among the most vulnerable areas in the province, prompting urgent calls for drought mitigation support from both the Western provincial government and the National Government.

Middle Fly acting disaster coordinator Jeremiah James told NBC News that relief supplies would be dispatched immediately, with formal impact assessments to be conducted during distribution.

“The plan from the Disaster Office is that we will not go and do assessments first. We are planning immediate relief supply needs,” James said.

item.title: Toroama reiterates Bougainville’s stand on independence

item.content:encoded:
Autonomous Bougainville Government [ABG] President Ishmael Toroama has reiterated that Bougainville’s push for self-governance is non-negotiable and cannot be diluted by administrative processes or performance benchmarks.

Speaking during the Joint Supervisory Body [JSB] meeting in Port Moresby on Wednesday, Toroama urged Prime Minister James Marape and the National Government to respect the 97.7 per cent vote for independence delivered in the 2019 Bougainville Referendum.

While acknowledging that Section 342 of the National Constitution gives the National Parliament the mandate to make the final decision, Toroama said the decision cannot be separated from the democratic mandate of the referendum.

He criticized the National Government’s formal position paper regarding a potential “non-affirming decision” by Parliament, stating that it is a masterpiece of bureaucratic evasion and historical revisionism.

He rejected suggestions that a parliamentary rejection would reset Bougainville back to an extended autonomy framework focused on drawing down powers and achieving fiscal self-reliance.

“Bougainville is moving away from the autonomy space, and let me make that clear,” Toroama said.

“The National Government is threatening our constitutional right to self-determination as if I were in a progress review or some corporate evaluation subject to an external yardstick that shifts political tides in the National Parliament.

“We do not need a clear pathway to revisit that question. The question has been asked, answered, and sealed in ink and blood.”

The President also raised concerns over decisions introduced in Parliament regarding a three-quarters voting threshold and specific timeframes, stating that these were made without joint consultation required under the Melanesian Agreement and the JSB resolution of Dec 5, 2025.

“Bougainville had no part in these decisions. As required by law, these were unilateral decisions made by the National Government and the Speaker of the National Parliament that affect our mandate,” he said.

He reminded leaders that the 2019 referendum was strictly supervised by the United Nations and certified by the current Speaker of Parliament, Job Pomat, during his tenure as Acting Governor-General.

He added that no objections or legal challenges were raised during the statutory 40-day appeal period following the certification.

Toroama confirmed that Bougainville’s stance is backed by the ABG House of Representatives, national MPs from Bougainville, and key regional accords including the Panguna Communiqué and the Buka Resolution.

He called on National MPs to fully embrace the Joint Consultation Report and the Melanesian Framework as the official roadmap forward, emphasizing that the UN and global partners continue to monitor the process.

“In the eyes of my people, there is legal justice and there is moral justice. With due respect, Prime Minister, Bougainville demands both,” Toroama concluded.

item.title: IPA launches awareness campaign in Milne Bay over new associations law

Official records show that of the 162 incorporated associations registered with the IPA in Milne Bay, only one group has successfully completed re-registration und
item.content:encoded:
The Investment Promotion Authority [IPA] has deployed a awareness team to Alotau in Milne Bay Province to educate local executives on the newly enacted Associations Incorporation Act 2023, which supersedes the previous 1966 legislation.

Official records show that of the 162 incorporated associations registered with the IPA in Milne Bay, only one group has successfully completed re-registration under the new legal framework.

The remaining 161 bodies are currently classified as unregistered and risk losing their legal status if they do not update their records.

IPA Company Examiner Andy Pomat said that failure to comply with the updated laws could disrupt operations for community and civil society groups across the province.

"All associations across Papua New Guinea have been removed from the central registry for re-registration. According to our records for Milne Bay, out of 162 associations, only one has re-registered," Pomat said.

"If you don't comply, we will strike off the association. Non-compliant groups will face financial penalties, which was not the case under the old act."

He said team members were assisting executives on the ground in Alotau to complete their documentation.

Re-registration is free during a one-year grace period. Groups that fail to re-register before the grace period expires on June 30, 2027, will be subject to penalty fees.

Executives seeking to register new associations can access the IPA digital portal at www.ipa.gov.pg.

Milne Bay marks the third province visited in the national outreach campaign, with the awareness team scheduled to travel to Maprik in East Sepik province next.

item.title: Western Highlands backs lifeline aviation as Rapa commits K200,000 to MAF
item.description: The Western Highlands Provincial Government [WHPG] has pledged K200,000 to the Mission Aviation Fellowship [MAF] PNG, recognising the organisation's 75 years of delivering life-saving services to some of Papua New Guinea's most isolated communities.
